reason: The Book of Ruth contains no violence whatsoever and presents no model of leadership based on violence toward unruly people. The leadership exemplified through Boaz and Naomi is characterized by kindness (hesed/חסד), generosity, wisdom, and justice administered through lawful means (the proceedings at the gate). Boaz demonstrates leadership through his fair treatment of workers, his protective care toward Ruth, his integrity in business dealings, and his respect for legal conventions. The narrative emphasizes covenant-keeping, loyalty, and righteous conduct as the markers of good leadership, explicitly contrary to any violence-based model.
